title: Customer signal microstories and solution proposals — Aug 2026
body:
Purpose: quick synthesis of recent customer conversations (May–Jul 2026) oriented to product hypotheses and concrete engineering proposals. This is a working doc: notes are intentionally terse, includes raw quotes, microstories, suggested fixes, and proposed owners.

Summary (one-liners):
- Recurring ask: predictable tail-latency for chat at scale (esp. 99th percentile) when bursts hit Dedicated pools.
- Cost signal: customers want clearer guidance on end-to-end cost tradeoffs for quantization + batching (real examples, not just % savings).
- Private deploy: audit log granularity and KMS rotation APIs are blocking for a few regulated customers.
- Developer ergonomics: faster local emulation / lower-friction model-swapping in dev environments.

Method: pulled transcripts from 18 customer calls, 32 CS tickets flagged as \"feature\", and two enterprise scoping workshops. Focused on issues that appeared in 3+ distinct accounts.

Microstories and raw quotes (representative):
1) Microstory: \"Fine-grained latency SLO for support chat\"
   - Customer: midsize fintech (Dedicated) running customer support bot with 1k qps median bursts to 6k.
   - Problem: occasional spikes push 99p latency from 150ms to >2s; business impact is poor CS agent handoff and user drop-off.
   - Quote: \"We need something we can point to — 'this route is protected by X SLO' — otherwise we can't trust it for customer-facing flows.\"
   - Current workaround: overprovisioning (reserve more GPUs) or route to hosted which raises cost/latency.

2) Microstory: \"Cost math for quant + batching is too abstract\"
   - Customer: startup with multi-embedding workflows for search ranking.
   - Problem: recommendations like \"apply dynamic batching + q4f16 quantization\" are fine, but they need sample invoices showing token counts, batching window, and expected $/month impact.
   - Quote: \"We tried quantization and saw weird hallucinations on a small prompt set — we rolled it back; we didn't feel like we understood the cost tradeoff.\"

3) Microstory: \"Private deploy auditing gaps\"
   - Customer: healthcare provider (Private/VPC).
   - Problem: compliance team requires immutable audit trails per-request and KMS key rotation events linked to each model invocation. Current audit logs show basic request/response metadata but not key rotation ties.
   - Quote: \"Until rotation events are clearly tied to requests, our security team won't sign off.\"

4) Microstory: \"Developer friction swapping models locally\"
   - Customer: dev team embedding different LLM variants into feature branches.
   - Problem: too many manual steps to emulate Redwood routing and fallbacks in local dev; CI makes it worse because tests hit different model variants.
   - Quote: \"We spend half a sprint trying to reproduce a routing fallback that only happens in prod. A local flag that simulates routing would save us days.\"

Theme synthesis (grouped):
A) Reliability & Observability (latency SLOs, traceability) — HIGH IMPACT, HIGH FREQUENCY
   - Signal: 12 accounts called this out explicitly; repeated ask for per-route 99p SLOs and clearer error budgets.
   - Root causes customers perceive: opaque request routing, burst behavior from autoscale, and insufficient stack traces tying errors to model variants.
   - Hypothesis: provide per-route 50/95/99 latency profiles + automated anomaly alerts mapped to model variant rollouts.

B) Cost transparency & deterministic examples — HIGH IMPACT, MEDIUM FREQUENCY
   - Signal: 9 accounts asked for concrete cost scenarios (e.g., daily/weekly/monthly sample bills for a given workload).
   - Customer need: step-by-step runbook or calculator showing token distribution, effective batching windows, and quantization quality tradeoffs.
   - Hypothesis: ship a \"Cost Playground\" template with reproducible notebooks and sample billing projections for common workloads (chat, embeddings, rerank).

C) Compliance primitives for Private deployments — HIGH IMPACT for narrow set (regulated)
   - Signal: 4 enterprise accounts blocking on audit depth, KMS rotation APIs, and customer-managed HSM integrations.
   - Hypothesis: extend audit schema and add mapping between KMS events and request ids plus a guided onboarding checklist for infosec teams.

D) Developer experience for model versioning and routing — MEDIUM IMPACT, MEDIUM FREQUENCY
   - Signal: dev teams want low-friction tools to reproduce routing decisions, fallback behavior, and local inference quality checks.
   - Hypothesis: create a local emulation CLI (redwood-local) that can replay sample routing decisions and mock fallbacks with a config file.

Suggested tactical feature proposals (short):
1) Per-route latency SLO pages (product + console)
   - Product: console view for each 'route' showing historical P50/P95/P99, model variants in that window, and flags when SLOs breach.
   - Minimum viable feature: historical graphs + a downloadable CSV; flagging tied to a new alert rule type in the console.
   - Owner: product-hosted-api + observability eng.

2) Cost Playground + reproducible notebooks
   - Product: three notebooks (chat, embeddings, rerank) showing sample token traces, batching windows, quant profiles, and sample billing. Make templates runnable on small datasets.
   - Marketing/Docs: turn one notebook into a short customer-facing walkthrough (playbook) for sales and AMs.
   - Owner: product-optimize + developer-experience.

3) Enhanced audit schema & KMS mapping for Private
   - Engineering: add optional fields to audit log entries (kms_key_id, kms_rotation_id, key_version_at_request) and an admin API endpoint to export rotation timelines.
   - Compliance: draft onboarding checklist and example policy language to provide to customer security teams.
   - Owner: private-deployments + security-and-compliance.

4) Redwood-local CLI emulation + snapshotting
   - Feature: local server that reads a small config describing routing rules, model variants, and a set of sample requests; produces deterministic logs and simulated latency distributions. Support a \"snapshot\" file that can be attached to tickets for reproduction.
   - Developer story: integrate into CI so failing test suites can attach the snapshot for triage.
   - Owner: developer-experience + console-and-tooling.

Prioritization recommendation (quick):
- Highest near-term ROI: Per-route latency SLO pages (addresses several churny renewals and risk for Dedicated customers).
- Medium: Cost Playground (helps expansion and reduces churn from starter/prototype customers).
- Lower but blocking for deals: Audit/KMS mapping for Private (important for a small number of high-value deals).
- Developer UX: Redwood-local (nice-to-have, accelerates debugging and reduces support load).

Open questions / risks:
- Data ingestion for per-route SLOs: can we attribute tokens and latency reliably to a single route when requests traverse fallbacks? (engineering feasibility/accuracy risk).
- Quantization quality guarantees: we need an eval harness to show expected quality degradation range for common prompts — otherwise customers will mistrust cost claims.
- Legal/compliance risk: exposing KMS key metadata could be sensitive; need security review and customer opt-in.

Immediate next steps (concrete):
- Week 0–2: product + eng sync to scope Per-route SLO quick spike (Alec + Priya). Deliver rough feasibility and list of required telemetry fields.
- Week 1–3: create Cost Playground prototype notebook for chat (Evan + docs). Share with 3 pilot customers for feedback.
- Week 2–6: security and private-deployments to draft audit schema changes and circulate for internal review (Maya to coordinate).
- Ongoing: attach this doc to account notes for flagged accounts (CS owners: assign tickets and reference snapshots).

Owners / point people:
- CS lead / synthesis owner: Maya Chen
- Observability + product SLOs: Alec Romero
- Cost / Optimize: Evan Brooks
- Private compliance: Priya Nair

Notes to self:
- When sharing with sales, include one-pager with anchors: sample $/month delta for a 500k token/day chat workload (before/after quant+batching) and expected P99 improvement scenarios.
- Keep a running list of tickets that include sample payloads for replay in the local emulator.

Appendix: short list of accounts to circulate prototypes to (internal names) — flagged for NDA before sharing:
- Nimbus Health (Private)
- HelixSearch (Dedicated)
- Paxion Support (Hosted/Dedicated mix)

Unresolved: need to confirm if audit schema changes require DB migration window. Add to engineering spike.

-- end working notes --
